newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end little changed.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged on Monday in thin trading as the market reached a new equilibrium, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 103.78
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.05 pct at 103.08
Volume was a low 105 million shekels with activity in the Makam falling to only 30 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds were mixed today. Yields on inflation-linked bonds fell from 5.25 percent in July to only 4.1 percent and the market is becoming more balanced now," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.

"Activity was very low and the market is mixed. Prices of CPI-linked bonds rose sharply during the last three to four months and investors are waiting for fresh news," said Roy Meir at Simodan Brokerage House.
Both traders said the Bank of Israel was expected to leave its key lending rate for March unchanged.
"Unlinked bonds and Makams rose slightly today. These bonds remained almost unchanged despite the rise of CPI-linked bonds and now they have to catch up," Kolka said.

Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher despite the rise of the shekel against the dollar. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3660 shekels against 3.3730 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
